A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of UniT, including Appendices A–E. Text, equations, tables and figures can be matched despite relocation, resizing and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation, editing and reasoning experiments in Tables 1–4, ablations in Tables 5–6, and generalization-preservation results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains the original UniT benchmark evaluations, cognitive-behavior and data-quality ablations, and Appendix C fine-tuning results.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the same data synthesis and filtering, Bagel training, nested text/image guidance, and budget-forced iterative inference. Relocated explanations do not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both use the same synthetic training coverage and evaluate OneIG-Bench-EN generation, CompBench multi-object editing, ImgEdit multi-turn editing, and MIRA visual reasoning. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 1–4, including Janus-Pro and BLIP3-o, the CompBench editing baselines, Bagel/Bagel+CoT, and GPT-5/Qwen2.5-VL (72B). Section 5.1 retains the same best-of-N comparison.

E3.justification: Both retain budgets C=1–10, a maximum of four refinement rounds per ImgEdit turn, the same evaluation metrics, and HPSv3 selection for parallel sampling. ImgEdit still uses 100 examples per method and three expert annotators.

E4.justification: The cognitive-behavior and data-filter ablations in Tables 5–6, generalization-preservation analysis in Appendix C, and qualitative and failure examples are retained. Moving examples and failure discussions to the appendices adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting remains unchanged, including averaging across annotators and Krippendorff’s alpha of 0.82 in Section 4.1. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval or significance reporting is added.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6, scaling plots and Appendix C retain their results. UniT’s overall scores remain 0.843 on OneIG, 0.988 on CompBench, 4.26 on ImgEdit and 11.5 on MIRA. Cropped or relocated illustrations preserve the same qualitative findings.

T1.justification: The nested CFG equations in Section 3.2 and computational-budget definition in Section 3.3 are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, propositions or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: unified multimodal test-time scaling, extrapolation to longer reasoning chains, sequential scaling efficiency, and benefits across generation, editing and reasoning.

C2.justification: Physics/spatial failures, verification hallucinations, conflicting subgoals, base-model capability limits and inference-cost caveats remain. The former Section 5.4 and conclusion caveats move to Appendix E; their substance and Appendix D’s scaling-limit interpretation are preserved.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same 12K trajectories, 700 H100 GPU hours, guidance scales, filtering thresholds, deduplication procedure and Table 7 prompt template. Implementation and resource-access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list retain the same cited works and research positioning. Relationships to earlier test-time scaling, unified multimodal models and multimodal chain-of-thought methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: Failure cases, limitations and future directions move to Appendix E, while a reflection explanation moves to Appendix B. The date, acknowledgements and cross-references receive small edits; most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The same nine figures and seven tables remain. v1 Figure 4 becomes appendix Figure 8; several displays are enlarged or repositioned, and Figure 1’s bird panels are cropped. These are limited display and layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: v2 preserves the method, empirical evidence, reproducibility information and substantive limitations. Enlarged displays modestly help legibility, while moving examples and caveats to appendices changes their prominence. These editorial adjustments do not establish a meaningful net change in overall paper quality.
